original.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to aviation turbine fuel (ATF) in India as of April 2026:
items: Value Added Tax on ATF in Delhi — 29%
Cap on April's domestic ATF base price hike — 25%
original.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
original.explain: Delhi charges 25% VAT on ATF; 29% is Tamil Nadu's rate. The excise duty is 11%, and the government capped April's domestic base price hike at 25% even as international fuel prices rose by over 100%.
original.source: Delhi charges 25% VAT on ATF, Tamil Nadu 29%.

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to aviation turbine fuel (ATF) in India as of April 2026:
items: Value Added Tax on ATF in Delhi — 29%
Cap on April's domestic ATF base price hike — 100%
rewritten.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
rewritten.explain: Only the first pair is correct, since the excise duty on ATF is 11%. Pair 2 is wrong because Delhi charges 25% VAT on ATF (29% is Tamil Nadu's rate), and pair 3 is wrong because the government capped April's domestic base price hike at 25%, while over 100% was the rise in international fuel prices. With state assembly elections underway, the Federation of Indian Airlines has sought a temporary suspension of the excise duty and cuts in state VAT rates.
rewritten.source: With state assembly elections underway, the government capped April's domestic ATF base price hike at 25% while international fuel prices rose by over 100%.
